items.summary: Protesters from Geef Tegengas stormed a construction site for a new Microsoft datacentre in Westpoort, Amsterdam, climbing a crane and lighting flares while clashing with police. The action was part of wider European resistance to AI-driven datacentre expansion, separate from the Stop Dirty Data Centres campaign whose members stayed outside the fence. Police said force was used and an officer slightly injured; activists claimed teargas.
items.title: Activists Storm Amsterdam Microsoft Datacentre Site

items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber, an AI model it says improves on earlier models at finding and validating software vulnerabilities. During testing the model found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws and built exploits for 948 Linux kernel bugs that could grant root access. OpenAI classified it as having Critical cybersecurity capabilities under its Preparedness Framework, up from High for its previous model.
items.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber vulnerability-finding model

items.summary: An MIT-developed method called CheMeleon shows that machine learning can outperform existing approaches when data on a target property is scarce. The team, including graduate student Akshat Shirish Zalte and Jackson Burns PhD '26, reported findings in the Sept. 14 issue of the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling. Pre-trained on molecular descriptors from a million PubChem molecules without consulting literature, CheMeleon was used by nine of the top 20 entries in an OpenADMET contest. Zalte noted inquiries began before peer review completed. The model reportedly came out on top across 58 test cases compared with other foundation and classical models.
items.title: MIT Team Unveils Data-Efficient Molecule Prediction Model

items.summary: Elon Musk funded at least $474 million for the 2026 midterms, but Democrats are projected to win 259 House seats and at least 54 Senate seats. The article argues that Congress can use its oversight powers—public hearings, subpoenas—to investigate DOGE’s job cuts and spending. Senator Richard Blumenthal said there is a web of potential corruption worth exploring.
items.title: Democrats Plan Oversight of Musk After DOGE Fallout

items.summary: This post introduces the Reshard collective, a new NCCL-based communication pattern designed to accelerate reinforcement learning weight refit. During RL post-training, model weights must periodically move from training GPUs to inference GPUs using different parallel layouts, creating large redundant payloads that grow with model size. The authors reformulate refit as resharding a distributed tensor between source and destination layouts, enabling each GPU to receive only its needed shard instead of full parameters. An open-source reference implementation is provided in the NVIDIA NeMo RL framework.
items.title: NVIDIA Introduces Reshard Collective for RL Weight Refit

items.summary: Zyphra has released ZYFA, an open-source Apache 2.0 library of prefill attention kernels in FP8 and BF16 targeting AMD Instinct MI355X (CDNA4) GPUs running ROCm 7.2.3 with PyTorch 2.12. On real model activations at sustained clocks, its FP8 kernels run 1.16-1.76x faster than AITER's default library, while BF16 roughly ties AITER (1.01-1.02x). Real-model gains fall short of Gaussian benchmarks because the MI355X clock depends on operand-bit flips; ZYFA runs at 1,628 MHz versus AITER's 2,108 MHz on Mistral-7B activations while still needing fewer cycles overall. FP8 error sits within a few percent of Composable Kernel and Triton, with KL divergence from fp64 lower than AITER's across full models. Zyphra notes cross-vendor comparisons are limited by differing inputs and clocks and that NVIDIA GPUs were not measured; it recommends benchmarking on real activations at sustained clocks.
items.title: Zyphra Releases ZYFA FP8 FlashAttention for AMD MI355X GPUs

items.summary: Swedish furniture retailer IKEA reported a third consecutive year of falling sales on Nov 6, citing war-driven cost increases and weak demand from budget-conscious consumers. Group sales reached €43.8 billion (S$63 billion) for the fiscal year ending Aug 31, down 2% versus 2025. CEO Jakub Jankowski said growth must return to make products affordable. Net profit fell to €1.4 billion from €1.5 billion in 2025.
items.title: IKEA CEO Vows Growth After Third Year of Sales Decline

items.summary: Binance suffered the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, with hackers draining roughly US$2.5 billion in a single transaction before ultimately taking about US$3.6 billion overall. According to security firm Blockaid, the thieves exploited EIP-7702, an Ethereum upgrade implemented in May 2025 that lets wallets grant software permission to move funds without separate authorizations for each transfer. The attackers paid around US$15 in network fees to set up this delegation and then moved large sums in one transaction, reducing their exposure. Binance confirmed the attack was sophisticated and said EIP-7702 played a significant role; it has revoked affected permissions and strengthened controls. The FBI attributes the theft to North Korea, which denies involvement.
items.title: Hackers Drain US$2.5b from Binance Using Ethereum Upgrade Shortcut

items.summary: At a November 6 ribbon cutting, Illinois leaders unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two with an Nighthawk r2 processor at the University of Chicago's Hyde Park Labs. Harley T. Johnson, CEO of the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP), called it possibly the most publicly visible quantum computer in the world. The machine supports the National Quantum Algorithm Center, created by the state under a $500 million investment. Officials highlighted decades of regional research talent and recent demonstrations, including one using 70 logical qubits that ran in about 15 minutes.
items.title: Illinois Unveils Quantum Computer in Chicago as Part of National Center Effort

items.summary: The Guardian editorial argues that this week’s midterms showed the political cost of the AI boom is arriving, citing a Wall Street wipeout of $3.2tn and crashes at Anthropic, Nvidia and for Elon Musk. It notes influential figures see reality-checking value in the sell-off while Democrats campaigned against datacentre costs to residents. The piece concludes that letting markets decide alone will deepen economic insecurity and political distrust.
items.title: Guardian editorial frames AI sell-off as democratic reckoning

items.summary: New research from Vals, an AI-capability measurement firm, finds open-weight models now nearly match the best closed ones at complex network hacking. In simulated scenarios on mock corporate networks, OpenAI's trusted-only Daybreak completed 81 percent of tasks while Chinese model DeepSeek finished 73 percent. Runners also cost less—$2 to $3 versus $17 to $46 in tokens for GPT-6-Sol. Vals researcher Nikil Ravi says frontier models are being matched by downloadable open ones, suggesting recent access limits may be moot and urging defenders to prepare within 6, 12 or 24 months. Edera's Alex Zenla called it a possible start of a dangerous landscape, though he noted closed labs likely hold stronger unreleased models.
items.title: Open AI Models Match Closed Ones in Network Hacking Tests

items.summary: Meta indefinitely delayed a planned change requiring business account users to permit extensive AI training on external websites linked from Facebook, following weeks of backlash. A Meta spokesperson told Reuters the changes were paused while engaging stakeholders and that existing terms remain in effect. Critics warned the vague language could let Meta ignore robots.txt preferences, crawl off-Facebook content for AI training, and avoid licensing fees; courts in Brazil and Norway blocked the terms via injunctions, and the UK's Competition and Markets Authority opened an investigation.
items.title: Meta delays AI-training terms update amid global pushback

items.summary: The Electrek Podcast previews its weekly episode on sustainable transport, highlighting discussion of Tesla ending the Cybertruck, rising electric vehicle sales in several key markets, and additional topics. The live show airs every Friday at 4 p.m. ET on Electrek's YouTube channel, with an accompanying post published afterward.
items.title: Electrek Podcast Covers Tesla Cybertruck Cancellation and EV Market Surge

items.summary: The author of a CleanTechnica post reports that Tesla and SpaceX lost $420 billion in market cap following the recent midterm election, which he frames as ironic punishment for Elon Musk's shift toward Republican politics. The piece argues Democrats historically supported clean technology policies benefiting Tesla while Republicans have not, then attributes Musk's political change to specific events including COVID-19 lockdowns, his wealth and tax concerns, his child transitioning, and being excluded from a Biden EV event. It notes Musk donated at least $447 million as the country's largest individual donor in this election, which it says failed about 99.99% of its goal. The author speculates Democrats may investigate or punish Musk for attacks against them but offers no verification that market values have changed since reporting. Figures are reported as stated by CleanTechnica without independent confirmation.
items.title: Tesla and SpaceX Market Cap Falls After Midterm Election

items.summary: After heavy storms, the Chicago River received billions of gallons of raw sewage. The Racine Avenue pumping station dumped more than 10 billion gallons this year alone—more than any time since 2019—and its North Branch counterpart added nearly 2 billion gallons to the north branch. Officials say intense rains force untreated wastewater into rivers to prevent flooding, despite decades and billions of dollars spent on the Deep Tunnel project. Experts warn the system cannot keep pace with intensifying storms, threatening wildlife and public health.
items.title: Chicago River Overflows With Raw Sewage After Storms

items.summary: Pat Gelsinger, former Intel CEO and now with Playground Global, told industry leaders at the International Trade Partners Conference that semiconductor companies have grown complacent. According to a Semafor review of his presentation, he said they are not paranoid enough about new technologies needed for AI performance gains.
items.title: Former Intel CEO Warns Chipmakers of Complacency

items.summary: On Friday, Nov 6, Google acquired a data center site in southeast Wyoming from AI infrastructure firm Crusoe, the developer said. The purchase followed Alphabet's $17-billion investment announced Thursday for its first Wyoming facility amid growing political opposition to such projects.
items.title: Google Acquires Crusoe Wyoming Data Center Site

items.summary: OpenAI's CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC that OpenAI will continue its US data-center expansion despite a Democratic midterm sweep raising scrutiny fears. The company dropped non-disclosure agreements with officials and shared construction plans publicly. While the market fell about $2.5 trillion on Thursday, tech firms like Google and ByteDance also pursue new facilities. Friar cited 70 per cent quarterly business growth as demand stays strong.
items.title: OpenAI Advances Data-Center Expansion Amid Political Backlash

items.summary: On Tuesday, Google announced changes that disable Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Google Search for K-12 accounts until administrators re-enable them; Chris Phillips said banned schools would see a message indicating search is unavailable. Critics including Sen. Bernie Sanders called it extortion, while New York City reached out to discuss the update further.
items.title: Google Threatens School Search Access Over AI Bans

items.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer arrested on Oct. 9 for concealing recording devices in an executive conference room, pleaded not guilty Friday at the federal courthouse in San Francisco according to Bloomberg and CNBC. His lawyer filed the plea before Magistrate Judge Peter H. Kang, and he was returned to custody afterward with his attorney declining comment per CNBC. The indictment charges intercepting oral communications; conviction could mean up to five years imprisonment plus a $250,000 fine followed by three years supervised release as stated by the department.
items.title: Former OpenAI Engineer Pleads Not Guilty in Bugging Case

items.summary: Carolyn Steedman, writing in a letters column, thanked Joe Dunthorne for his investigation of the book club scam. She said she receives two or three such emails monthly and once forwarded one to report@phishing.gov.uk after replying to a sender claiming 500 members would read her books before requesting a fee for distribution. Three other readers replied with their own complaints about recent columns, including Peter Coltman questioning coverage of historical events and Huw Morgan worrying an author might catch cold in the rain.
items.title: Reader thanks journalist for exposing book club scam

items.summary: Two large UK milk processors cut farmgate prices, intensifying pressure on dairy farmers already selling below production cost after a volatile year of drought and high fuel and fertiliser costs. Freshways announced a 7p-a-litre reduction to 29.4p from 1 December, almost undoing earlier increases it had introduced in summer; its managing director Bali Nijjar cited stabilising global markets and rising costs. Arla Foods also cut its standard price by 0.45p to 40.41p while holding organic prices at 58.25p. The NFU called the Freshways move “hugely disappointing,” while farmer Ian Harvey said confidence is “at rock bottom.” Analyst Chris Walkland attributed the cuts to a global oversupply dating back to August 2025 and noted farmers struggle to switch processors easily.
items.title: UK Milk Processors Slash Farmgate Prices Amid Sector Pressure

items.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council announced plans to expand winter support, including new community shops in Pendeford, Graiseley and Bilston. About 17,000 people used the network over six months. Council leader Stephen Simkins said residents still face difficult bill choices. More than 135,000 received cost-of-living support while more than £18.5m was distributed. The council also launched a three-year financial wellbeing strategy and expanded its Community Chefs programme into schools.
items.title: Wolverhampton Council Expands Winter Support for Residents

items.summary: A healthcare information sharing and analysis center, Health ISAC, issued a security bulletin warning the industry about a wave of cyberattacks on refrigeration controllers that included an incident affecting a major French blood bank. The alert emphasizes operational technology attacks intersect with health-sector threats to patient safety. On Thursday, U.S. cybersecurity agencies published a fact sheet identifying industrial refrigeration and cold-chain systems as critical targets. Investigators consider Iran or Russian-aligned groups responsible, though claims remain unverified due to lack of access logs. Experts warn patching is difficult because downtime risks lifesaving supplies like blood and vaccines.
items.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry after French blood bank cyberattack

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that Stephen Miller, described as his most controversial aide and architect of the immigration crackdown, would become White House chief of staff days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections. The appointment replaces Susie Wiles, 69, who reportedly resigned Thursday night and was praised by Trump for an outstanding job. Trump said he wanted to make a change and called Miller one of his most trusted advisors. Critics responded sharply, with Democratic congresswoman Becca Balint calling it sickening that Trump promoted the architect of some of the administration’s worst decisions after voters rejected its policies.
items.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV has begun his longest overseas trip yet, a 12-day journey across three countries that marks his first major visit since lung cancer surgery to remove part of his right lung. Vatican officials say he finished his two-week recovery and needs no further treatment. The tour starts in Uruguay — famously Latin America's most secular nation, where around 3.5 million people live and only about a third identify as Catholics — before moving to Argentina and ending with a homecoming to Peru, where the pope spent two decades as a missionary priest and bishop of Chiclayo until becoming a naturalized Peruvian in 2015.
items.title: Pope Leo Opens South American Tour in Uruguay After Lung Surgery

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that Stephen Miller, his longtime hardline immigration advisor and domestic policy ideologue, would become chief of staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026. The appointment replaces Susie Wiles, who resigned Thursday night after controversy over her daughter Katie’s $35,000-a-month contract with a lobbying firm tied to the Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Trump made the announcement on his platform Truth, thanking Wiles for her service. At 40, Miller is described as one of the administration’s most despised figures by Democrats, whose hardline views may strain relations with the newly Democratic-controlled Congress.
items.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff

items.summary: The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights asked a court to hold Guatemala responsible for the violent eviction of 14 Maya Q’eqchi’ communities in Alta Verapaz, which cleared land for sugarcane plantations and destroyed traditional crops. The IACHR’s referral said evictions used disproportionate force and left residents without food or safe return. Disputes over unland-titled territory date to at least 2005; a court authorized the removals in 2011 after protests, prompting officials’ claims of threats to governability.
items.title: Guatemala Held Before Human Rights Court Over Indigenous Evictions

items.summary: Democratic Party figures say they will investigate corruption accusations against the Trump administration, with a focus on its ties to wealthy Middle Eastern countries. President Trump's businesses reportedly earned about $2 billion in income during 2025, roughly triple the previous year, partly from cryptocurrency firm World Liberty Financial, which was sold largely to an investment firm backed by UAE official Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Critics allege connections that the administration denies. Kushner and other deals face scrutiny over conflicts of interest. Ethics watchdogs argue some arrangements create improper influence. Senator Elizabeth Warren said her party would examine related matters including a presidential library project, while investigative journalist Matthew Cole's book alleges Kushner accessed roughly $2 billion in bank accounts through Middle East work he denied.
items.title: Democrats Prioritize Middle East Corruption in Trump Probe

items.summary: CMG reported that China launched remote sensing satellites 07-09 of the Yaogan-51 group from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center in Sichuan Province on November 5, 2026. The three satellites rode a Long March-2C carrier rocket into their preset orbits successfully and are used for scientific experiments and electromagnetic environment detection. The launch marked the 675th mission of the Long March rockets.
items.title: China Launches Yaogan-51 Remote Sensing Satellites

items.summary: A Nigerian Federal High Court voided the nomination of African Democratic Congress presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar and dissolved the party's leadership. The court ruled that interim chairman Nafiu Bala Gombe, rather than David Mark, should have led the party after its former chairman resigned in 2025. ADC officials called the ruling a calculated attempt to weaken their candidacy ahead of elections scheduled for 16 January. Abubakar said he would still contest and listed himself on the electoral commission's candidate list with Rotimi Amaechi as running mate, while Peter Obi expressed concern over uncertainty three months before voting.
items.title: Nigerian Court Voids ADC Presidential Nomination Ahead of January Poll

items.summary: Spain's Maritime Rescue Service rescued about 700 of the roughly 854 migrants it assisted aboard seven small fishing vessels off El Hierro since early Friday morning. Around 350 were transferred to Tenerife on a scheduled ferry, with another 350 planned for an afternoon crossing to ease pressure on reception facilities. Several people required hospital treatment; their exact countries of origin have not yet been established.
items.title: Spain Rescues Nearly 1,000 Migrants Off El Hierro

items.summary: An ABC News article reports that South Australia's political divide over a proposed hyper-scale data centre in Tungkillo, near Mannum, has united the Greens and One Nation at a community rally. The project by Melbourne developer Quantum DC faces strong local resistance over environmental, energy and water concerns. Mid Murray Council Mayor Simone Bailey said it was hard to understand the proposal's benefits, while independent MP Rebekha Sharkie posted that data centres do not belong on prime agricultural land. Premier Peter Malinauskas says law reform is needed before facilities can proceed unless they meet state standards.
items.title: SA Labor warned as data centre opposition unites Greens and One Nation

items.summary: A City of Casey Council survey found that community and family connection was the top factor making residents feel safer, outranking police patrols and CCTV. Besima Goga, a jeweller in Berwick's south-east Melbourne electorate, described break-ins leaving her boss injured and said she now shops with fear. Monash University political scientist Zareh Ghazarian noted voters also weigh infrastructure, crime handling, cost of living and housing affordability. The seat is held by Labor on a 4.7 per cent margin but could lie on a Coalition path to victory. Neighbourhood Houses Victoria CEO Keir Paterson said state funding for local houses had fallen behind costs with capacity at a ten-year low. Early voting begins November 18 before election day on Saturday, November 28.
items.title: Berwick Voters Prioritise Community Safety Over Crime Measures

items.summary: FRANCE 24 reports that the Republican Party's midterm defeat has left Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky optimistic about continued support, though he noted Democrats are 'speaking very clearly about supporting Ukraine.' However, analysts caution Congress faces limited scope due to Trump's retained foreign policy authority. James M. Lindsay of the Council on Foreign Relations explained that while the incoming Democratic Congress will be more supportive than the Trump administration, translating preferences into policy remains difficult because the president alone decides negotiation terms.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Loss and Its Implications for US-Ukraine Support

items.summary: Donald Trump appointed Stephen Miller, age 41 and current deputy chief of staff, as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Trump announced the change on Truth Social, calling Miller one of his most trusted advisors. The appointment comes days after Republicans lost control of both chambers in the midterm elections, amid scrutiny following immigration-enforcement shootings in Minneapolis. Wiles will move to Trump's political operation.
items.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff

items.summary: At the ninth China International Import Expo and Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai on November 5, 2026, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called for joint efforts to achieve balanced trade. He urged greater market openness, deeper investment cooperation, innovation, removal of trade barriers, and making 'the economic pie bigger together' through consultation.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Calls for Balanced Trade

items.summary: NetLab UFRJ, a Brazilian research group, reports that Meta likely interfered in Brazil's 2026 election. The group created the Big Tech Observatory during the campaign to monitor algorithmic recommendation and political advertising against Electoral Supreme Court rules. It found that between July and September, Meta received approximately R$ 2 million (US$ 400,000) for running 1,613 foreign-placed ads favoring or harming candidates — an estimate hedged by uncertainty over exact figures. The group also identified hundreds of restricted-period ads, fake profiles promoting a nonexistent 'digital vote,' the temporary disabling of Lula's campaign page on September 23, and signs that Lula's campaign may have paid between 33% and 43% more than Flávio Bolsonaro's to reach equal audiences. Meta rejected interference accusations on October 16, attributing the page block to an 'incorrect anti-fraud review.' The group noted transparency limits prevent definitive conclusions about pricing mechanisms.
items.title: Brazilian Research Group Accuses Meta of Election Interference

items.summary: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are set to make their public debut at Zoo Atlanta on Friday, Nov. 6. The zoo plans an exclusive unveiling of the animals from China. Dr. Gina Ferrie, Vice President of Collections and Conservation, will discuss how her team prepared for the event.
items.title: Zoo Atlanta prepares giant pandas for public debut in November

items.summary: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the 65,000 expected by economists, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%. Markets then priced an 85% probability of a quarter-point Fed increase at its December 8-9 meeting, up from around 75%, and moved expectations forward to April. Analysts say the data strengthens the case for tightening as inflation stays above target.
items.title: Strong US jobs report lifts Fed rate-hike bets

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported on Friday that Microsoft is winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle as part of a broader reassessment of billions of dollars in cloud partnerships, citing people familiar with the matter. The report says Microsoft has been turning off rented capacity after declining to renew the contract, and notes Oracle shares fell nearly 3% while Microsoft was little changed.
items.title: Microsoft Wind Down Oracle AI Computing Deal Amid Cloud Review

items.summary: Nashik police named AIMIM leader Imtiyaz Jaleel an accused in a supplementary chargesheet filed Friday for allegedly helping key accused Nida Khan while she was absconding. A lawyer representing one of the victims said the notice under section 35 (3) of the BNSS had been served around a month ago, and that Jaleel did not appear; further proceedings will follow legal procedure. The SIT is probing nine cases dating to July 2022 at TCS's Nashik unit, which maintains a zero-tolerance policy on workplace harassment.
items.title: TCS Nashik Police Name AIMIM Leader in Supplementary Chargesheet

items.summary: Delhi Police registered an FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms, following directions from the National Human Rights Commission. The Special Cell filed it under Sections 67 and 67B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, after about 10 links were flagged in a complaint. NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo confirmed the action.
items.title: Delhi Police Register FIR Over Alleged CSAM Circulation on Meta Platforms

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to increase Cybercab output. The move follows weaker-than-expected sales, recalls and price changes; US 2025 sales reached 20,237 units, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, far below Musk's 2023 target of 250,000. Tesla has issued 11 Cybertruck recalls since late-2023 deliveries began.
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production for Cybercab at Texas Factory

items.summary: Nisha Bhagat, an Adivasi leader and social activist aged around 38 in Ranchi, died by hanging at her residence after alleging harassment during a roughly 10-minute livestream. She had called the Pithoria police inspector while live before being rushed to hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival; her body went to RIMS for post-mortem. Police said no suicide note was recovered and an investigation is underway.
items.title: Adivasi Leader Found Dead After Alleging Harassment on Facebook Live

items.summary: Anthropic reported nearly $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier, per an amended IPO filing disclosed this month as the company prepares for a potential listing. 'Big Short' investor Michael Burry raised concerns about the figures, writing that the company is priced for optimism and betting its existence on it. He pointed to falling sales-marketing expenses and channel-partner revenue dropping from 48% in early 2026 to nearly 40%. Anthropic said the decline stemmed from lower partner-sourced revenue and changes in distribution terms. Separately, AI-linked stocks fell after Democrats won control of Congress.
items.title: Michael Burry questions Anthropic IPO figures amid AI stock selloff

items.summary: Farooq Abdullah called rebel MLAs’ demands genuine, while Omar Abdullah repeatedly offered to resign amid the National Conference’s worst internal challenge in decades. The rebels sought to replace eight ministers and remove adviser Nasir Aslam Wani; those demands stayed unresolved. Leaders agreed consultative committees per minister and a manifesto committee for election promises, including J&K’s special status. Farooq dismissed split talk, calling the party “united and strong,” while an MLA said all strengthening demands were accepted.
items.title: NC Leaders Defuse Rebel MLA Crisis With Talks and Resignation Offer

items.summary: The Department of Posts announced that India’s only floating post office, housed on a houseboat at Nehru Park on Dal Lake in Srinagar, will now stay open from 9am to 9pm. The extension raises its hours from five to 12 and follows increased footfall and public demand for services beyond regular times, according to chief postmaster general Col Sagar Hanuman Singh.
items.title: India’s Only Floating Post Office Extends Its Hours

items.summary: FIIs increased their buying of Indian equities, investing a net Rs 34,584 crore over the past five trading sessions. On Thursday alone they poured in Rs 14,975 crore, marking the biggest single-day FII purchase in more than a year. This follows months of selling as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to sell.
items.title: Foreign Investors Boost Indian Equity Buying on Friday Amid Market Rally

items.summary: Trump administration health officials are expected to miss President Trump's Sunday deadline for new childhood vaccination recommendations, according to people familiar with the matter. Kennedy had promised plans by Nov. 8 but said they would be delivered as ready rather than on schedule. The delay comes amid the largest measles outbreak in decades across 45 states, with 5,182 cases recorded and six deaths confirmed nationally.
items.title: Trump Health Officials Miss Vaccine Recommendation Deadline Amid Measles Outbreak
